title: TRACED Act: The 5 Sections That Matter for Outbound Calls
meta_description: The TRACED Act lets the FCC propose robocall fines without a warning and adds up to $10,000 for intent; in 2024 the FCC collected no section 227 forfeitures.

image.takeaway: In 2024 neither the FCC nor the Attorney General collected a section 227 forfeiture or criminal fine.
image.alt: Hero card for an article on the TRACED Act: in 2024 neither the FCC nor the Attorney General collected a forfeiture or criminal fine for violations of section 227 of the Communications Act, according to the FCC’s report to Congress.

chart.source: Basis: FCC report to Congress under the TRACED Act, 23 December 2025 (DA 25-1100). Source: fcc.gov, November 2026.
chart.alt: Bar chart of informal complaint counts to the FCC alleging section 227(b) robocall violations by calendar year: 38,657 in 2020, 46,189 in 2021, 39,436 in 2022, 31,042 in 2023 and 33,137 in 2024. One complaint may be counted under several sections. In 2024 the FCC issued one section 227 forfeiture order, in a caller ID case, and no section 227 forfeiture or criminal fine was collected.
